text.p: Three months after its merger with Ionian Insurance, Metrolife is moving into bankassurance capitalising on Commercial Bank's extensive branch network, its chief executive said.

"Metrolife-Commercial believes its competitive edge will rest on the development of bankassurance. Thus, the first phase of its co-operation with Commercial Bank is being implemented," managing director George Kapouranis told reporters.

Metrolife insurance consultants will now be present in 80 out of Commercial Bank's 330 branches, he said. Two initial bankassurance products -- a retirement and a child savings programme -- will be introduced.
Based on a five-year business plan, the company intends to expand business abroad with Germany as the first target.
Metrolife-Commercial expects that 40 percent of its revenue will be derived from bankassurance by the year 2001. Its target is turnover of 40 billion drachmas and a market share of 10 percent.
The company expects 1996 and 1997 to be loss-making years following its merger with Ionian Insurance but it will turn profitable in 1998, Kapouranis said.
"The unification of the networks is of utmost interest to us. There are banking products that may be sold through Metrolife's network," said George Michelis, general manager of Commercial Bank.

Metrolife is planning a 2.5 billion drachma rights issue to finance its business plan. It will issue 3,503,718 new common registered shares at 700 drachmas. Rights will entitle shareholders to one new share for every four outstanding.
